comparison: Both evaluate claims about antalarmin preventing morphine-induced sociability deficits in male mice (C1, C38, C40, C41). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides more detailed statistical justification, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the finding with editor noting 'solid' strength of evidence. High agreement.

Perfect match on claims C2, C43, C44 regarding antalarmin's ineffectiveness in female mice. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence (lack of interaction), while peer reviewers confirm the sex-specific pattern. Complete agreement on this key sex difference.

Both address genetic validation using CRF1 KO mice (C3). OpenEval also includes detailed gene-dosage claims (C58-C62) not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm CRF1 receptor involvement through genetic approach. Strong agreement on genetic validation.

OpenEval R3 addresses both behavioral (C3) and electrophysiological (C58-C62) gene-dosage effects. Peer R6 focuses on confirming CRF1 involvement through genetic approach across both measures. Substantial overlap in claims C58-C62. Both SUPPORTED with agreement on genetic validation strengthening pharmacological findings.

Perfect match on claims C4, C50-C52 regarding antalarmin preventing morphine-induced PVN activation in males. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical power (n=110 cells), peer reviewers note 'rescue to control levels' with 'solid' methods. Complete agreement.

Perfect match on claims C5, C53, C56 regarding antalarmin's ineffectiveness in female PVN neurons. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides cell count details (n=93), peer reviewers accept as part of sex-specific pattern. Complete agreement on electrophysiological sex differences.

Perfect match on claims C6, C58-C62 regarding gene-dosage effects on PVN firing. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes graded response across genotypes, peer reviewers confirm genetic validation of CRF1 involvement. Complete agreement on genetic evidence.

Perfect match on claims C7, C57, C63 regarding mechanistic link between behavioral and neural measures. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes correlative nature lacking direct causation, peer reviewers accept as 'potential mechanism involving oxytocin neurons.' Agreement with OpenEval more cautious about causal inference.

Perfect match on claims C8, C65-C67 regarding cell-type-specific effects in male OXY/AVP neurons. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details immunohistochemical identification (40 cells), peer reviewers note these mechanistic insights were added in revision and strengthen the work. Complete agreement.

Perfect match on claims C9, C68 regarding cell-type specificity (OXY/AVP vs. AVP-only) in males. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes differential effects suggesting OXY-specific modulation, peer reviewers accept as part of mechanistic framework. Complete agreement.

Perfect match on claims C10, C70 regarding lack of antalarmin effect on female OXY/AVP neurons. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with other sex-specific findings, peer reviewers accept as part of overall sex-difference pattern. Complete agreement.

Perfect match on claims C11, C71 regarding lack of antalarmin effect on female OXY-only neurons. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval contrasts with male-specific effects, peer reviewers accept without challenge. Complete agreement on sex-specific cell-type responses.

Perfect match on claims C12, C72 synthesizing sex-specific CRF-OXY interactions. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanisms remain speculative, peer reviewers explicitly highlight 'sex-specific role' as key finding. Agreement with peer reviewers more emphatic about significance.

Perfect match on claims C13, C48 representing main conclusion about sex-linked CRF1 involvement. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of evidence, peer reviewers describe as 'valuable findings' with 'solid' evidence. Complete agreement on core conclusion.

Perfect match on claims C14, C128 regarding therapeutic implications. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval details multiple gaps (acute vs. chronic, male-only effects, translation uncertainty), peer reviewers note interest for addiction field but don't endorse therapeutic claims. Complete agreement on uncertain translational relevance.

Perfect match on claims C46-C47, C49, C90 regarding dissociation between locomotor and sociability effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes potential indirect effects, peer reviewers implicitly accept through endorsement of 'solid' methods. Agreement with OpenEval slightly more cautious.

Perfect match on claims C73, C76 regarding morphine impairing sociability similarly in both sexes. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions whether sex has 'marginal role' given mechanistic differences, peer reviewers accept as context for CRF1 sex-specificity. Agreement with OpenEval more nuanced about interpretation.
